headline: Comerica integration lifts profit, credit quality improves
summary_short: Fifth Third's Q2 2026 net income available to common shareholders was $763M ($0.83 diluted EPS), up from $128M ($0.15) in Q1 as Comerica contributed a full quarter of results, while the net charge-off ratio improved to 0.30%, the lowest level since 2Q23.
summary_long: Net income of $801M (+385% q/q, +28% y/y) reflected the first full quarter of consolidated Comerica results, driving net interest income up 14% q/q to $2.22B (NIM +6bps to 3.36%) and noninterest income up 18% q/q to $1.06B. Diluted EPS was $0.83; adjusted EPS was $1.02 excluding $0.19 of merger-related and other one-time charges ($203M pre-tax merger costs). Noninterest expense fell 12% q/q to $2.11B as Q1's larger one-time merger charge rolled off. Provision for credit losses fell to $129M from $227M (Q1 included an $83M Day-1 Comerica allowance build); net charge-offs improved to 0.30%, the lowest since 2Q23. CET1 rose 4bps to 9.93%; no share buybacks in H1 2026.

drivers.explanation: CEO Tim Spence called Q2 'another step toward the earnings power we committed to deliver,' citing fee-business momentum, NIM expansion, and an on-track Comerica integration (systems conversion set for Labor Day weekend).

Net interest income and noninterest income both rose primarily on the addition of Comerica for a full quarter, plus organic loan production and fee-business growth in wealth management, commercial payments, and capital markets.

Not itemized separately; tracks the net income narrative of full-quarter Comerica consolidation revenue growth outpacing merger-related expense, with a lower q/q provision for credit losses also contributing.

Full-quarter Comerica consolidation lifted net interest and fee income; q/q gain also reflects Q1's $83M Day-1 Comerica credit-loss allowance build not recurring, partly offset by continued merger-related charges.
Diluted EPS rose on higher net income, though growth was diluted by roughly 10% more weighted average diluted shares q/q and 36% more y/y, issued as Comerica merger consideration.
Basic EPS tracks the same net income growth and Comerica-related share dilution as diluted EPS; not separately narrated in the release.
Not explained in the release; cash and equivalents rose to $4,374M with no accompanying cash-position narrative in this press release.
Release attributes the y/y increase to ~$4.2B of new long-term debt tied to the Comerica acquisition; this quarter's sequential decline is not itself explained in the release.
Release attributes higher wholesale funding, including short-term FHLB advances (+$3.3B q/q), to bridging a seasonal trough in commercial deposit balances.

Y/y growth reflects roughly $12.7 billion of common equity issued as Comerica merger consideration in Q1 2026 plus retained net income; this quarter's equity roll-forward shows no new acquisition-related issuance, just net income less dividends.
Share count rose on shares issued as consideration for the Comerica acquisition, which closed earlier in 2026.
